_about: Written by studies/theory/paper/build_facts.py from the committed round files. Each entry: value, n, unit, source, note.

_row_fields.kind: r1_hand_matched | heldout_claim (rounds 2-3, the main score there) | offline_test (rounds 4-7, the main score) | carried_duel_row (round 6: a promoted rival's round-5 duel tests, 'readers' = the theory it replaced) | heldout_filter_claim (rounds 4-7, survivors only, not in the headline) | exposed_claim (round 2, left out by the engine)
_row_fields.theory: id as in the round files
_row_fields.r1_*/r2_*: reader 1 and 2 (interval null where none was filed)
_row_fields.gain: recomputed, clipped to [-3, 3]; null without reader intervals
_row_fields.nearer: w theory nearer than the readers' mean, t tie, l readers nearer (site rule); null when not compared
_row_fields.nearer_both: theory strictly nearer than each reader
_row_fields.flags: headline (in the 403), compared (in the 394), reader_intervals (in the 236), carried, exposed, tie, within_noise, leak_context (round 2: readers and new authors had a commit subject with result numbers in context), divergent (both readers' centres outside the theory's interval)

predictions_filed.note: round 1: the 7 hand-matched interval predictions; rounds 2-3: claims on scored held-out targets; rounds 4-7: offline predictions the engine scores (fits, zeros by construction and one failed replication left out), carried duel rows of round 6 included. Per round: {"1": 7, "2": 151, "3": 80, "4": 42, "5": 48, "6": 71, "7": 27}

predictions_computed.note: filed minus 23 offline predictions with no number (missing packages, rows or fields). Per round: {"1": 7, "2": 151, "3": 80, "4": 29, "5": 45, "6": 67, "7": 24}

predictions_compared_with_readers.note: computed minus the 9 carried duel rows of round 6, whose comparison is the theory they replaced, not a reader

predictions_with_reader_intervals.note: compared minus rounds 1-2, where the readers filed point forecasts only; log gain and reader coverage exist only here (rounds 3-7)

distinct_quantities_compared.note: rounds 2-3: several theories claim the same target. Distinct per round: {"1": 5, "2": 38, "3": 29, "4": 29, "5": 45, "6": 58, "7": 24}

proposed.note: distinct ids over rounds 1-7; includes 3 promoted rivals (r5-m03-rival, r5-m10-rival, r6-account-rival) and 1 account (r6-account); the planted control is not counted. New per round: {"1": 6, "2": 10, "3": 10, "4": 10, "5": 10, "6": 9, "7": 8}

entries_per_round.note: carried theories count in each round they were scored in

forecast_runs.note: nearer here = nearer than BOTH readers of the same run (the forecast page's rule). Measured values were read from board posts by a model job (forecast_score), not by a script. Whether each forecast was committed before its result was posted needs the board and git history and is not recomputed here (the site literal says 10 of 25).

value.1: lib/check.py: a predictor given each theory guesses 58 held-out board numbers (points, no intervals); score = closer/farther counts against 2 no-theory predictors; one planted reversed theory.
value.2: lib/v2.py: each author files value + 90 % interval per held-out target; score = divergent wins minus losses (both readers outside the interval), against a reversed copy; exposed targets left out; published mechanisms imported.
value.3: lib/round.py: headless jobs in empty directories; readers file intervals too; score = log gain in nats against the mixture of the 2 readers, clipped to [-3, 3], with a bootstrap interval; held-out items no earlier round used.
value.4: offline tests become the main score: 12 pairwise different mechanisms, each with 3-6 predictions and exact recipes fixed by sha256 before any row is read, computed by scripts from stored per-problem rows; 2 no-theory readers predict the same numbers; held-out claims can only remove a theory.
value.5/5.1: rival stages: a blind agent writes the strongest other mechanism and tests where the two differ; gain = theory minus rival log density; 5.1 adds a second turn and a +-2 nat decision rule.
value.6-6.3: stage account: one budget of the base-to-RL gap whose shares sum to 1, tested like a theory; 6.1 at least 3 cells; 6.2 null cell, fits and zeros by construction not scored, replicate stage; 6.3 --account-from; 'within noise' no longer counts as outside.
value.7/7.1: experiments stage (each side predicts the other's GPU experiments, ranked by separation per GPU minute); 7.1: a duel test where the defender's centre is inside the rival's interval adds 0 and a win needs 2 separating tests; carried duel wins kept out of round totals; account only with --with-account.
value.8: forecasts inside the round (targets_open, forecast): theories and readers forecast the open work items; no round run with it in these files.

value.round-07/run.json: no per-stage model recorded in run.json

models.note: Only the CLI aliases 'opus' and 'sonnet' are recorded; no run file holds a dated model id. Theories, readers, rivals, defenders, test writers and reviews: opus. Targets (reading held-out numbers off board items): sonnet. Round 1: predictors and the planted theory sonnet, generators opus. Round 3 reversal text: sonnet.

right_where_readers_wrong.statement: Because Olmo-3 RL-Zero-Code 3.0 was trained with truncated rollouts masked rather than punished, it learned a runaway long-generation mode (the looping seen on LiveCodeBench) that at T 1.0 on MATH-500 drives its longest problems to the 16,384 cap, so Code 3.0 carries Code 3.1's math gain on short problems but loses it, and falls below the cued base, on the longest quartile.
